sections.title: A diverse genus
sections.text: Salvia contains annual and perennial herbs, subshrubs and shrubs. Depending on species, plants range from compact forms around 20 cm to border plants near 2 m; most have aromatic leaves.

sections.title: Flowers and plate
sections.text: The flowers are tubular with two lips and grow in spikes or looser clusters. The plate shows wrinkled, aromatic-looking leaves and violet, two-lipped flowers characteristic of a sage, but the genus-level name does not identify a species.

sections.title: Food and caution
sections.text: Culinary sage is specifically Salvia officinalis; its leaves are used as a herb. That use cannot be generalized to every Salvia species, so the pictured genus-level plant should not be assumed edible.
